newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks gain early, aided by OTC interest.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks gain early, aided by OTC interest.

text.p: Singapore stocks garnered more momentum early Thursday on pent-up demand for Malaysian issues and institutional buying of blue chip stocks, dealers said.
Volume was an impressive 160 million shares after only an hour of trade and turnover was seen likely to match Wednesday's 530 million shares, or Singapore $910 million in value, by day's end.

"There's a lot of stockist activity out there for small cap stocks but also keen interest in Singapore banks and property," a dealer with a local bank said. The Straits Times Industrials Index climbed 25.53 points to 2,253.17 at 0230 GMT.
While overall action was in Malaysian over-the-counter (OTC) stocks, fuelled by post Lunar New Year demand, fund managers were also eyeing selected blue chips.
"Some banks have been re-rated and the price gaps between them are narrowing," the dealer said.
Top gainers included the foreign tranche of UOB, up Singapore $0.60 to S$17.40, Oriental Holding up S$0.40 to S$13.60 and City Development, up S$0.50 at S$15.50.
Sri Hartamas topped the actives, up S$0.05 to S$1.31, and Insas Berhad, up S$0.03 at S$1.20.
